justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are comprehensively covered: Patient & EMR Service handles registration and EMR records; Scheduling Service with Redis Redlock resolves resource clashes; Billing Service with Claim Submitter formats X12 EDI claims; and Audit & Compliance Sidecar enforces immutable audit trails.
justifications.performance_efficiency: EMR screen load under 1s P95 is achieved via Redis Enterprise caching, Elasticsearch CQRS read models, PgBouncer connection pooling, and PWA Client IndexedDB caching, while ClickHouse handles heavy analytical query offloading.
justifications.compatibility: The dedicated HL7 FHIR Adapter Container supports standardized FHIR APIs, resources, and terminology mapping (LOINC/SNOMED-CT). The DICOM & Document Processing Container ingests DIMSE/DICOMweb imaging, and Billing Service integrates ANSI X12 EDI processors.
justifications.usability: Patients, Clinical Staff, and Administrators are served via the responsive PWA Client Container, which provides offline synchronization and Web Push notifications. However, specialized UI workflows for the distinct user roles are bundled into a single generic client container.
justifications.reliability: Active-active 99.99% availability is supported by CloudNativePG multi-master/synchronous replication, Redis CRDT geo-replication, Kafka MirrorMaker 2 across hybrid regions, WireGuard/BGP automatic failover, and Envoy circuit breakers. WORM storage ensures 10-year retention.
justifications.security: Rigorous security includes MFA/OIDC at API Gateway Container, AES-256 field/disk encryption backed by HSM/PKCS#11, OPA fine-grained ABAC, Envoy mTLS 1.3 mesh, and tamper-evident audit streaming to WORM storage for HIPAA and GDPR compliance.
justifications.maintainability: Domain services (EMR, Scheduling, Billing, FHIR) are cleanly isolated microservices with loose coupling via Kafka and RabbitMQ. Cross-cutting concerns are modularized into Envoy mesh, OPA authorization, and audit sidecars, supported by OpenTelemetry.
justifications.portability: The entire stack uses Kubernetes-native, cloud-agnostic components (CloudNativePG, MinIO, Strimzi Kafka, WireGuard hybrid gateway) running uniformly on on-prem-k8s and AWS eu-central-1 without proprietary cloud-provider lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Multi-tier caching with Redis, Elasticsearch CQRS read models for EMR searches, and connection pooling via PgBouncer ensure concurrent reads bypass transactional database contention to meet P95 < 1s.
sensitivity_points: Redis cache hit ratio and Elasticsearch index synchronization latency.
PgBouncer connection pool sizing under sudden burst concurrency.
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency between PostgreSQL write path and Elasticsearch read model.
Increased memory overhead across Redis Enterprise nodes.

PERF-02.justification: The HL7 FHIR Adapter uses rate limiting, BullMQ, and asynchronous Kafka/RabbitMQ event buffering, completely decoupling ingestion spikes from the read path and PostgreSQL/Elasticsearch serving EMR screens.
sensitivity_points: Kafka partition throughput and consumer group processing capacity.
Memory buffering limits in BullMQ and Redis under peak ingest.
tradeoffs: Asynchronous ingestion trades immediate cross-system consistency for UI read performance.
Additional infrastructure complexity running dual message brokers (Kafka and RabbitMQ).

AVAIL-01.justification: GTM and WireGuard hybrid tunnels facilitate traffic failover, with active-active Redis CRDTs and MirrorMaker 2 replicating data; however, cross-region multi-master PostgreSQL synchronization poses split-brain and failover latency risks within 60 seconds.
sensitivity_points: Cross-region network latency and bandwidth across the hybrid WireGuard tunnel.
Health check interval and DNS TTL configured in the GTM.
tradeoffs: Strict database consistency across regions vs failover recovery time within 1 minute.
Network encryption overhead over hybrid site interconnects.

AVAIL-02.justification: CloudNativePG Raft consensus provides automated sub-30-second failover, while the Billing Service’s state machine (XState) and persistent messaging queues allow transactional claim retries without duplication.
sensitivity_points: CloudNativePG failover and election timeout configuration.
Idempotency keys and transactional boundaries in claim state machines.
tradeoffs: Synchronous database replication latency vs zero data loss guarantee on failover.
Slight transaction delay during Raft leader re-election.

MOD-01.justification: Claim submission and EDI formatting are isolated entirely within the Billing Service container's Claim Submitter component, keeping changes localized while leaving the Patient & EMR Service completely untouched.
sensitivity_points: Coupling level between clearinghouse-specific EDI formats and claim submission models.
Modularity of the ANSI X12 state machine implementation.
tradeoffs: Custom formatting logic per clearinghouse vs unified internal canonical claim model.
Independent deployability of Billing Service vs shared integration schemas.

MOD-02.justification: Changes are confined to the PWA UI component, Patient & EMR Service controller/validation schemas, and database schema, with the sidecar transparently capturing audit logs.
sensitivity_points: JSON/relational schema migration agility in PostgreSQL.
Ajv schema validation maintenance in Fastify controllers.
tradeoffs: Strict schema validation overhead vs frictionless demographic field evolution.
Automated auditing via sidecars vs domain-specific explicit audit annotations.

SEC-01.justification: The API Gateway mandates MFA alongside OAuth2/OIDC, stopping single-factor logins, while the Observability Collector and Alertmanager immediately trigger real-time SIEM alerts via mTLS webhooks.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of non-bypassable MFA policies at the ingress gateway.
Alertmanager notification latency when dispatching security webhooks to SIEM.
tradeoffs: Strict rate limiting and authentication steps vs login user experience.
Increased latency introduced by gateway-level credential verification and security checks.

SEC-02.justification: Fine-grained OPA authorization evaluates access rules, while pgaudit and the Audit Sidecar cryptographically sign every access event via HSM, streaming to immutable WORM storage retained for 10+ years.
elements: Compliance Archival Gateway & WORM Object Storage
sensitivity_points: Rego policy evaluation latency on the hot data access path.
HSM throughput when cryptographically signing continuous high-volume audit records.
tradeoffs: Granular per-request ABAC/audit latency vs strict HIPAA compliance.
High storage cost of 10-year immutable WORM audit logs vs audit durability.
